title: Bioceramics: are they osteoinductive?
topic: MTA-type calcium silicate cements are biocompatible and osteoconductive; osteoinduction: cell-culture signals only, ectopic bone not shown.

claims.source: Torabinejad & Parirokh, J Endod 2010;36:190-202 (PMID 20113774); Gomes-Filho et al., J Endod 2009;35:256-60 (PMID 19166785); Moretton et al., J Biomed Mater Res 2000;52:528-33 (PMID 11007621): subsided to 'mostly moderate' under rat skin; abstracts

claims.claim: 5 of 6 root ends: complete cementum over MTA · monkey · 5 months (animal histology)
claims.source: Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1997;23:225-8 (PMID 9594770); abstract: 'five of six root ends filled with MTA had a complete layer of cementum over the filling', 3 monkeys

claims.claim: AMALGAM billboard, shown for the whole beat: inflammation stays; cementum on the cut dentin, none over the filling (picture only)
claims.source: Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1997;23:225-8 (PMID 9594770); abstract: all amalgam root ends inflamed; cementum 'had not formed over the root-end filling material, although it was present over the cut root end' (amalgam count not stated, so none shown)

claims.claim: OSTEOCONDUCTIVE · bone grows on the surface · MTA implanted in bone (animal histology)
claims.source: Definition: Albrektsson & Johansson, Eur Spine J 2001;10 Suppl 2:S96-101 (PMID 11716023). Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1998;24:468-71 (PMID 9693572): guinea-pig tibia, direct bone apposition most often with MTA, no frequency given; abstracts
Sarkar et al., J Endod 2005;31:97-100 (PMID 15671817); abstract: hydroxyapatite-like layer on MTA in phosphate-buffered fluid
Albrektsson & Johansson, Eur Spine J 2001;10 Suppl 2:S96-101 (PMID 11716023); abstract: recruitment of immature cells and their stimulation to develop into preosteoblasts

claims.claim: CELL CULTURE · BMP-2, ALP, osteocalcin rise; Ca²⁺ wired to BMP-2 only
claims.source: Maeda et al., J Endod 2010;36:647-52 (PMID 20307738): human PDL cells, 2 donors, calcium from MTA and BMP-2. Wang et al., Cell Prolif 2014;47:241-8 (PMID 24635197): rat mandibular marrow stromal cells, MTA 0.02 mg/ml, ALP and osteocalcin up; abstracts. Schematic: dials show direction only, all needles at the same height. Results vary with extract dilution and cell type: MTA-conditioned medium lowered osteocalcin in mouse PDL and marrow progenitors (Vidovic Zdrilic et al., J Periodontal Res 2017;52:1058-67, PMID 28691752; abstract)

claims.claim: NON-BONY SITE · rat · subcutaneous · mineral chips, no bone (picture) · stamp ECTOPIC BONE: NOT SHOWN (animal histology)
claims.source: Moretton et al., J Biomed Mater Res 2000;52:528-33 (PMID 11007621); abstract: subcutaneous MTA in rats, 15-60 days, dystrophic calcification, no osteogenesis. Strict test: Barradas et al., Eur Cell Mater 2011;21:407-29 (PMID 21604242); abstract, which also says rodents show limited, if any, bone induction by biomaterials, hence 'not shown' rather than 'cannot'

claims.claim: Verdict (MTA-type calcium silicate cements): BIOCOMPATIBLE ✓ tissue tolerates it (animal + human histology) · OSTEOCONDUCTIVE ✓ bone grows on it (animal histology)
claims.source: Claims 1-4 above; human pulp histology: Nair et al., Int Endod J 2008;41:128-50 (PMID 17956562). 'Tissue tolerates it' follows Williams DF, Biomaterials 2008;29:2941-53 (PMID 18440630); abstract: the material 'shall do no harm to those tissues'. All in vivo studies shown used MTA

claims.claim: Verdict: OSTEOINDUCTIVE ? cell-culture signals · ectopic bone: not shown
claims.source: Maeda 2010; Wang 2014; Moretton 2000 (rat, the only study found that reports directly on bone at a non-bony site); Barradas 2011 (as above)

caption:
Are endodontic bioceramics osteoinductive? Depends on the definition.
Biocompatible: yes. Cementum covered MTA in 5 of 6 monkey root ends, 5 months (amalgam: none).
Osteoconductive: yes. Bone forms directly on MTA in bone.
Osteoinductive: in culture BMP-2 (PDL cells), ALP, osteocalcin (marrow cells) rise. Strict test, bone at a non-bony site: not shown. Under rat skin: mineral, no bone; rats are a weak model, no large-animal test found.
Mostly MTA data. Schematic animation.
Refs: Albrektsson 2001 Eur Spine J; Barradas 2011 Eur Cell Mater; Torabinejad 1997, 1998, Maeda 2010 J Endod; Wang 2014 Cell Prolif; Moretton 2000 J Biomed Mater Res.
